evidence_set: 1383 people with DSM-IV alcohol dependence, recruited by advertisements and clinical referrals at 11 US academic sites and abstinent for 4 to 21 days, were randomized to 9 groups: medical management (9 sessions with a health care professional) with naltrexone, acamprosate, both or two placebos, each with or without a combined behavioural intervention (CBI) delivered by specialists in up to twenty 50-minute sessions, or CBI alone without pills or medical management. People with other substance use disorders (except nicotine or cannabis) in the last 90 days (6 months for opioids) or by urine drug screen, or with psychiatric disorders requiring medication, were excluded. The research assistants who assessed drinking were not blinded to psychosocial treatment.

evidence_set: The authors interpret the short palpebral fissures as secondary to deficient growth of the eyes (microphthalmia noted at birth in patients 1 and 7), the maxillary hypoplasia as producing relative prognathism, and the joint and palmar-crease changes as possible consequences of limited movement or aberrant position early in fetal life; of the five children with a cardiac anomaly, three were considered to have had a ventricular septal defect that closed before 1 year of age. The paragraph calls the pattern this syndrome; the paper nowhere uses the name fetal alcohol syndrome.
